segments.english:
11049 — Hassana al-Muzaniyya,⁵

Her name had been Jathama.

Abu Umar transmitted her story with an isnad through Salih ibn Rustum, from Ibn Abi Mulayka, from Aisha, who said: “An old woman came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he said—”

segments.arabic:
لها: «من أنت»؟ فقالت: أنا جثامة المزنية. قال: «كيف حالكم؟ كيف أنتم بعدنا»؟ قالت:
بخير، بأبي أنت وأمي يا رسول اللَّه! فلما خرجت قلت: يا رسول اللَّه، تقبل على هذه العجوز هذا الإقبال؟ فقال: «إنّها كانت تأتينا أيّام خديجة، وإنّ حسن العهد من الإيمان» «١» .
قال أبو عمر: هذا أصحّ من رواية من روى ذلك في ترجمة الحولاء بنت تويت.
قلت: سيأتي بيان ذلك في الحولاء غير منسوبة.
segments.english:
He said to her, “Who are you?” She replied, “I am Jaththama al-Muzaniyya.” He said, “How are you all? How have you been since we left?” She replied, “Well—may my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah!” When she departed, I said, “O Messenger of Allah, do you show this old woman such attention?” He replied, “She used to visit us in the days of Khadijah, and faithful observance of old ties is part of faith.” (1)

Abu Umar said: This is sounder than the narration of those who related it in the biography of al-Hawla bint Tuwayt.

I say: An explanation of this will appear under al-Hawla, with no nisba given.
